rows.what the ink shows: The left of the zero contains an additional upright with a leftward foot, but its top merges with the oval and its bottom with cancellation, so the independent bracket outline cannot be recovered cleanly. At the right endpoint the surviving glyph has two upward-open cusp/bowl shapes, most clearly a large opening at the right; this differs from the same-page infinity comparator, whose two lobes are closed. A diagonal also crosses the left bowl and its base is thickened. Omega is a plausible surviving/overwritten form, but the crossed layers and both endpoint delimiters cannot be separated securely. The original whole-interval uncertainty is retained; this does not certify infinity.

The target contains a left brace-like double curve, an open crescent across the upper right, a descending oblique stroke into the central junction, and a doubled hooked foot. The clear 4 after prop. lower on this page instead has a short descending stem, rightward elbow, and bent terminal downstroke. The target therefore is not a clean copy of that 4. A 5-like upper contour is visible in a composite/overwritten figure, but the order and full outline of its layers are not distinguishable; I cannot safely replace the uncertain numeral with a determinate numeral.

The erased heading retains the capital C, low rounded following strokes and the paired tall l ascenders seen in the upper Corollaire heading. At the far right a separate high hooked stroke rises above the cancelled word body, curves down, and finishes with a short rightward basal foot. Its height and curved top/downstroke distinguish it from the low final e in the clear upper heading and support a terminal numeral 2. The middle/ending letters are substantially crossed but the word outline and paired ascenders support Corollaire.
